blocks.text: The ABO system was discovered by Landsteiner in 1901. He found two antigens on red blood cells (RBCs): antigen-A and antigen-B. He observed some individuals have antigen-A on their RBCs while others have antigen-B. He also observed that many individuals do not have any of these antigens. Later, Landsteiner’s students discovered that some individuals have both A and B antigens on their RBCs. So, they named the different blood groups as:

items: People with antigen-A — blood group A
People with antigen-B — blood group B
People with both (antigen- A & antigen-B — blood group AB
People with neither of antigen-A & antigen-B — blood group O

blocks.text: Each person’s blood plasma contains antibodies against the antigen s/he does not have:

items: Blood group A → anti-B antibodies
Blood group B → anti-A antibodies

blocks.text: This is called Landsteiner’s rule of antigen–antibody relationship.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: Some people secrete antigens A and B in body fluids e.g., saliva, tears, urine. They possess a dominant secretor gene “Se” on their chromosome 19.
Inheritance of the ABO Blood Groups

The ABO system is controlled by the gene I (“I” stands for iso-haem-agglutinogen). It is located on chromosome 9 and has multiple alleles i.e., Iᴬ, Iᴮ and i. The alleles Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant over each other. While allele i is recessive to both of them. The Iᴬ allele produces antigen-A, the Iᴮ allele produces antigen-B. Allele i does not produce any antigen. Therefore;

items: Genotypes IᴬIᴬ and Iᴬi produce antigen-A. This phenotype is called blood group A. Individual’s plasma contains anti-B antibodies.
Genotypes IᴮIᴮ and Iᴮi produce antigen-B. This phenotype is called blood group B. Individual’s plasma contains anti-A antibodies.
Genotype IᴬIᴮ produces both antigen-A and antigen-B. This phenotype is called blood group AB. Individual’s plasma does not contain anti-A or anti-B antibodies.
Genotype ii produces neither antigen-A nor antigen-B. This phenotype is called blood group O. Individual’s plasma contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: In ABO system, the production of anti-A and anti-B antibodies does not require any exposure to antigens. Rather, these antibodies start forming from embryonic life and continue throughout life.

items: A person has blood group A while his wife has B. They have four children each with different blood group. Explain that how is it possible?
A woman with blood group B has a child with blood group O. What are the genotypes of the mother and child? Which genotypes could the father not have?

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: In pea plants, each character that Mendel studied was controlled by a gene with two alleles. One allele was completely dominant over the other. But incomplete dominance and co-dominance do not obey this rule of dominance. Similarly, in multiple allelic system, a gene has more than two alleles, any two of which work for producing a phenotype.

blocks.text: Principle of Transfusion in ABO System
During blood transfusions between two incompatible (unmatching) blood groups, the recipient’s antibodies attack the antigens on donor’s RBCs. It causing clumping (agglutination) of RBCs. It happens;

items: If blood group A individual receives blood group B and vice versa, and
If donor’s blood group is AB and the recipient is A, B, or O.
O blood group (donor): has no antigen-A and antigen-B. So, it can be given to A, B, AB, or O. So, O blood group are called universal donors of ABO system.
AB blood group (recipient): has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies. So, it can receive all blood types. So, AB group are called universal recipients of ABO system.

blocks.text: Justify why a recessive blood group allele ‘i’ is more frequent in the population.

items: In a cross between blood group O (ii) and O (ii), all offspring will have blood group O (ii).
In a cross between heterozygous Iᴬi and Iᴬi, 25% offspring will have blood group O (ii)
In a cross between heterozygous Iᴮi and Iᴮi, 25% offspring will have blood group O (ii).
In a cross between heterozygous Iᴬi and Iᴮi, 25% offspring will have blood group O (ii).

blocks.text: That’s why blood group allele ‘i’ is more frequent in the population.
